rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about or consider criminal history until after a conditional offer, and may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer, only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods may be considered, with an individualized assessment and written reasons if the offer is withdrawn.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer; look-back 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd), 1 yr (4th); $1,000/$5,000/$10,000 penalties
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.effective_date_note: Approved June 18, 2021; takes effect first day of the seventh month next following enactment, computed as 2022-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units. Limited exceptions for methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units offered by housing providers.
rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 first violation; up to $5,000 with one prior violation in 5 years; up to $10,000 with two or more prior violations in 7 years. Enforced by the Division on Civil Rights; no court action by private persons; may require return of application fee.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

parsed.doc_summary: Official text of NJ P.L.2021, c.110, the Fair Chance in Housing Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 et seq.), restricting criminal-history screening of rental applicants; effective 2022-01-01.
